source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Choose a fair representative basis for comparing two datasets instead of relying only on the largest value, total, or count of wins when the comparison context changes.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Total is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Choose a fair representative basis for comparing two datasets instead' is answered as total rather than representative value.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Total is what produces representative value, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Choose a fair representative basis for comparing two.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is representative value because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Choose a fair representative basis for comparing two datasets instead' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: representative value is settled by running 'Decide whether a prompt or claim is statistical by checking whether it': A statistical statement is a claim or summary expressed with numerical values — on the item about Choose a fair representative basis for comparing two.

intelligence.enrichment: Data can be compared using different features such as maximum, minimum, total, average, and range, but totals are not appropriate for comparing groups of different sizes; a per-item average can balance highs and lows.
